full_reasoning:
Loop 5 of the aggressor-flow-gate / full-trace arm. Full prior context loaded: loops 1-4 full_reasoning + metrics blocks, plus the full text of execution_algos/afg-f-l1/NOTES.md, afg-f-l2/NOTES.md, afg-f-l3/NOTES.md, and afg-f-l4/NOTES.md. Total context_chars_in = 73257 (~18314 tokens).

Prior context recap (compressed). Loop 1 added min_gross_volume=8.0 floor: pnl -9.18% vs base. Theory ('thin-tape one-sided prints are noise') falsified; IS/P&L decoupling first documented. Loop 2 tightened flow_threshold 2.0->1.5: every metric byte-identical to base. Root cause: MES size is integer-valued, _net_flow is integer-valued; thresholds in (1, 2] all produce identical skip sets. Methodological lesson: integer-equivalence classes; threshold tests must cross integer boundaries. Loop 3 tightened 1.5->1.0 (crossing into class (0, 1]): pnl +10.39%, sharpe +0.836. Validated loop 1's mechanism. Level-threshold lever saturated at threshold=1 (threshold=0 is degenerate). Loop 4 halved window_seconds 10.0->5.0: pnl -0.34% vs base (-9.72% vs loop 3). Root cause: at 5s the deque is often empty (warm-up path), and when non-empty |net_flow| over 5s is more dominated by single-print noise. Gate became mostly no-op + residual skips noisier. Durability hypothesis won decisively over freshness.

Targeted change for this loop (single behavioural knob, after correction): (1) revert window_seconds 5.0->10.0 (correction of loop 4's known-harmful default; not the hypothesis under test); (2) lengthen window_seconds 10.0->15.0 (the hypothesis under test). flow_threshold=1.0 and min_gross_volume=0.0 preserved unchanged. Net delta vs afg-f-l4: window 5.0->15.0. Loop 4's forward-looking note made this the priority-1 direction explicitly.

Expected effect: pnl +8% to +14% vs base if durability continues to help (modest improvement on loop 3's +10.39%); roughly equal to loop 3 (+10%) if saturation reached; +0 to +5% vs base if degeneracy has set in (gate fires too often). Trade count slightly lower than loop 3 (-0.5 to -2%); sharpe tracks P&L; IS worse than loop 3 if more skips remove favorable-fill entries.

What actually happened: durability continues to help, decisively. realized_pnl=1421.25, +13.20% vs base (upper end of predicted range), +2.54% vs loop 3 (best-in-arm). sharpe=6.732, +1.138 vs base, +0.302 vs loop 3 (best-in-arm). trade_count=104836, -2.20% vs base, -0.55% vs loop 3 -- skip set expanded modestly as predicted, well within the selective-gate regime. No sign of the degeneracy floor loop 4 warned about (where anti-cascade alternation would force trade_count toward ~50% of base). Max drawdown -0.0306% -- best in arm (-0.0027 pp better than base, -0.0018 pp better than loop 3). Win rate +0.04 pp (essentially unchanged). is_weighted_bps +1.30% vs base (slightly worse) but -3.53% vs loop 3 (notably better) -- the longer window's gate is more selective per skip (more samples = higher per-skip evidence quality), so the formerly-skipped favorable-fill entries become a smaller share of skipped trades. The IS/P&L decoupling documented in loops 1, 3, and 4 is *partially relieved* here: IS is roughly base-equivalent while P&L is the highest in the arm.

What this teaches: the durability mechanism extends past 10s. Loop 4 established 10s > 5s; loop 5 establishes 15s > 10s. The two loops together pin down the direction of the optimum to (10s, 20s+) and rule out (<10s). The combined operating point (window=15, threshold=1) beats loop 3's (window=10, threshold=1) on P&L, sharpe, and drawdown simultaneously while bringing IS back to roughly base-equivalent -- a near-strict improvement on every axis the experiment tracks. The level-threshold lever (saturated at loop 3) has now been complemented by a window-length improvement.

Methodological consolidation across loops 1-5. Three structural levers identified and probed: (a) gross-volume floor (loop 1: harmful, large min_gross_volume); (b) flow_threshold (loops 2-3: 2.0 inert no-op, 1.0 large positive; lever saturated at integer floor); (c) window length (loops 4-5: shorter is worse, longer (so far) is better; not yet saturated). The unexplored levers are: asymmetric thresholds (loop 1 suggestion #2), flow acceleration / first-difference (loop 1 suggestion #3, structural change escaping integer-quantisation), and a hybrid small floor at the new operating point (loop 4 suggestion).

Directions for loop 6 (in priority order with loop 5's evidence applied):

  1. **Continue lengthening: window_seconds=20.0** at threshold=1.0, floor=0.0. The natural extrapolation of loop 5's positive result and the test loop 4 flagged as the degeneracy boundary. Either outcome is informative: if P&L improves, durability curve still rising and loop 7 pushes to 25-30s; if P&L flattens or falls, 15s is at/near the optimum and the degeneracy regime has begun. Loop 5's trade_count headroom (-2.20% vs base) means the gate would need to compress trade_count to ~80-90k (~15-25% cut) before anti-cascade alternation dominated; so 20s is a clean diagnostic test point.

  2. Hybrid small gross-volume floor at (window=15, threshold=1): min_gross_volume=2 or 3. Re-examines loop 1's premise at the materially different operating point established by loops 3-5. Lower priority than (1) because (1) is more mechanistically clean and directly extends this loop's finding. Loop 1's negative result was strong but the parameter context has shifted.

  3. Asymmetric thresholds at (window=15, threshold=1): e.g., BUY=1, SELL=2 across the integer boundary. Less prioritised because the symmetric gate has just produced the best result in the arm -- the asymmetric variant would have to outperform a now-strong baseline.

  4. Flow acceleration / first-difference (loop 1 suggestion #3, never tried). Structural change escaping the level-threshold paradigm. Highest information value but highest implementation risk; defer until simpler levers stop yielding.

What NOT to try in loop 6: any further window shortening (empirically inferior per loop 4); any non-integer-boundary threshold tweak at threshold=1 (per loop 2's discretisation lesson, still applies); large min_gross_volume (per loop 1's strong negative).

Methodological note for the experiment as a whole. This loop closed a clean two-loop sub-experiment on window length: loop 4 established the freshness/durability fork and proved freshness loses; loop 5 ran the orthogonal lengthening test and proved durability continues to win past 10s. The two loops together pin down the direction of the optimum and rule out the entire (<10s) region. Both loops depended on the full-trace context channel -- loop 5 needed loop 4's microstructural diagnosis (empty-deque warm-up path, per-skip SNR argument) to make 'lengthen the window' the obvious next step rather than abandoning the window lever after one negative result. A metrics-only mode looking at loop 4's -0.34% might have moved to a different lever entirely; the full trace led directly to the highest-leverage move available, which produced the best result in the arm to date. The information value of the full-trace channel compounds: loop 4's near-zero result was 'inert in metrics' but 'rich in lesson', and loop 5 converted that lesson into +2.54% P&L on top of loop 3.
